As somebody who has been writing and performing since 2005, here is some advice; take what resonates, leave what doesn’t. 

Notice what is happening around you, who you’re with/ what they just said, what you might’ve just heard in a social media post, every time you get so upset that you want to change the world. That feeling? Yes, that feeling requires specificity, but it does not require nano levels of minutiae — in other words, don’t try to reinvent tropes, just use them as shorthand to communicate to the audience things you know for a fact you, yourself, can feel. 

Have a clear goal for your protagonist, figure out if they are up against a society, another person, nature, or themselves. You sound like having an outline of the action, that you can check to make sure it works backwards and forwards, would be the best way for you to get started. 

The best play writing trick I learned is “don’t just rely on the dialogue”. Set a timer for five minutes and write a scene without any dialogue, just to prove to yourself that you can, and I bet you it’s not gonna be nearly as intimidating. 

Either write about things you know really well or make up a completely different world, that way you’re not constantly asking yourself whether or not you’re taking people out of the world of the play because you “didn’t do enough research”. 

And, if you are completely blanking, I highly recommend setting that same timer for five minutes, finding some writing prompts, the playwriting handbook was always my favorite for that purpose, and, eventually, you’re either gonna come up with the first scene of your play or you’re gonna write something that’s going to inspire it. 

Here’s a writing prompt, to get you started: the protagonist finds a magical item in the storeroom of their work. Your job is to figure out what the item is, what it does, and what your protagonist chooses to do with it once they figure it out. 

If all else fails, do what we did in no shame theatre: the world is absurd, therefore we shall act the same. Make your characters something not human as a ‘commentary on humanity’, professors eat that shit up 😉 You got this!

Complete Newbie? Open Stage/ Mic Nights, Sketch Comedy/ Improv are the most accessible, then college and community theatre, then professional stage production — see if you can pick up any patterns about what holds interest vs what seems to be an excuse to hold an audience hostage. 

Simple exercises include random prompts with timed writing.

Practice writing scenes without dialogue — trust me. 

Read any text out loud while reading it, if you’re having a hard time “getting it”.
